variable_coverage.construction: ΔFINC: Difference between the high- and low-Ψ pools’ future-earnings incremental explanatory power estimates within a two-digit SIC industry-year. Each group’s FINC is the unrestricted Equation (4) R² less the restricted current-earnings regression R². Reported formula: ΔFINC_{i,t} = FINC^H_{i,t} − FINC^L_{i,t}. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔΨ: Differential relative firm-specific return variation: the high-Ψ minus low-Ψ group ratio of summed residual sums of squares to summed total sums of squares from weekly firm-return fits, aggregated within each two-digit SIC industry-year. High/low firms are selected as the two top and two bottom firm-year Ψ values within each constituent four-digit SIC industry. Reported formula: ΔΨ_{i,t} = Ψ^H_{i,t} − Ψ^L_{i,t}; each Ψ^g_{i,t} = Σ_{j∈g}Σ_w ε²_{j,w,t} / Σ_{j∈g}Σ_w(r_{j,w,t}−r̄_{j,t})².. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

I: Industry-structure control: square root of the number of firms used to construct the future earnings-response and return-variation measures in the two-digit industry-year; the paper defines it using the number of constituent four-digit industries. Reported formula: I_{i,t} = sqrt(2 n_{i,t}), with n_{i,t} the number of four-digit industries in two-digit SIC industry i in year t.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔS: Difference between the high- and low-Ψ pools' size controls. Section 3.2.1 equation (16) defines each pool measure as the average of log inflation-adjusted total assets, while Table 1 and Table 5 describe it as the log of average inflation-adjusted total assets; the exact order of averaging and logging is unresolved. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔD: Difference between high- and low-Ψ pools’ asset-weighted average diversification. Firm diversification is the number of distinct four-digit lines of business reported in Compustat’s Industry Segment file; weights are total assets. Reported formula: ΔD_{i,t} = D^H_{i,t} − D^L_{i,t}; D^g_{i,t} = Σ_j A_{j,t}s_{j,t}/Σ_j A_{j,t}.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔVE: Difference between high- and low-Ψ groups’ two-digit-industry averages of firm-level five-year standard deviations of past earnings-per-share changes. Earnings changes are scaled by the previous year-end price. Reported formula: ΔVE_{i,t} = VE^H_{i,t} − VE^L_{i,t}; firm volatility is stdev(ΔEPS_t/P_{t−1}) over the prior five years.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔVβ: High-minus-low difference in the two-digit industry beta-volatility control. The Section 3.2 prose says each firm’s standard deviation across twelve monthly CAPM betas is averaged across firms; Table 1 instead says the measure is a simple average of monthly-beta variances within a corresponding four-digit industry. The source does not resolve this aggregation conflict. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔINS: Difference between high- and low-Ψ pools’ two-digit-industry institutional ownership, weighted by firm total assets. Annual firm ownership is the simple average of quarterly ownership; missing ownership values are set to zero. Reported formula: ΔINS_{i,t} = INS^H_{i,t} − INS^L_{i,t}.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔR&D: Difference between high- and low-Ψ groups’ two-digit-industry total-assets-weighted ratios of research and development expenditures to total assets. Reported formula: ΔR&D_{i,t} = R&D^H_{i,t} − R&D^L_{i,t}.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

Δr: Difference between high- and low-Ψ pools’ two-digit-industry value-weighted stock returns in year t−1. Reported formula: Δr_{i,t} = r^H_{i,t−1} − r^L_{i,t−1}.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔFD: Difference between high- and low-Ψ groups’ R² values from fits of current earnings changes on current and one-, two-, and three-year-ahead dividend changes. DIV is dividends per share plus stock-repurchase value over common shares outstanding; ΔDIV is set to zero if a firm neither pays dividends nor repurchases shares. Reported formula: ΔFD_{i,t} = FD^H_{i,t} − FD^L_{i,t}.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

r_t − r_{f,t}: Firm daily return minus the daily T-bill rate. The source defines the daily rate as the simple rate that compounds over the calendar days in the month to the one-month T-bill return. Reported formula: r_t − r_{f,t}. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

r_t − r_{m,t}: The paper's printed RHS return input is firm daily return minus the value-weighted market return. This is retained exactly as printed, although unusual for a CAPM equation. Reported formula: r_t − r_{m,t}. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

r_t: Current total annual stock return, defined as capital gain plus dividend yield and computed from Compustat. Reported formula: [(split-adjusted fiscal-year-end share price + split-adjusted dividends during the year) / split-adjusted previous fiscal-year-end share price], as stated in footnote 8.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔE_t: Current-year change in EBITDA (operating income before depreciation) per share, divided by the beginning-of-fiscal-year market value of common equity; item 13 differenced against prior year and scaled by prior-year price times shares. Reported formula: ΔE_t = [Compustat item 13_t − item 13_{t−1}] / [P_{t−1} × shares_{t−1}]. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

r_t: Current total annual stock return, defined as capital gain plus dividend yield and computed from Compustat. Reported formula: [(split-adjusted fiscal-year-end share price + split-adjusted dividends during the year) / split-adjusted previous fiscal-year-end share price], as stated in footnote 8.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔE_t: Current-year change in EBITDA (operating income before depreciation) per share, divided by the market value of common equity at the beginning of the firm’s fiscal year. The paper’s equation-specific wording for future ΔE uses the beginning price of the current year; the timing convention for future terms is therefore unresolved. Reported formula: ΔE_t = [Compustat item 13_t − item 13_{t−1}] / [P_{t−1} × shares_{t−1}]. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔE_{t+1}: One-year-ahead change in earnings per share (operating income before depreciation over common shares outstanding), scaled by the price at the beginning of the current year P_t−1, as Equation (4) explicitly states. Reported formula: ΔE_{t+1} = (EPS_{t+1} − EPS_{t+0}) / P_{t−1}. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔE_{t+2}: Two-year-ahead change in earnings per share (operating income before depreciation over common shares outstanding), scaled by the price at the beginning of the current year P_t−1, as Equation (4) explicitly states. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔE_{t+3}: Three-year-ahead change in earnings per share (operating income before depreciation over common shares outstanding), scaled by the price at the beginning of the current year P_t−1, as Equation (4) explicitly states. Reported formula: ΔE_{t+3} = (EPS_{t+3} − EPS_{t+2}) / P_{t−1}. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

design_coverage.reason: Construct the original firm-year universe by CRSP/Compustat matched records from 1983–1995; delete non-10/11 CUSIP suffix duplicates; assign SIC from the sales-largest business segment; exclude financials and utilities; require uninterrupted weekly-return years; then build four-digit high/low and two-digit industry-year pools.
Use dated GVKEY–PERMNO links and dated segment/company identifiers; sampled fields do not establish historical link completeness.
The baseline uses time-random effects; no fixed-effect dummy family is reported. The time-random-effects panel/year grouping and industry-year inputs are part of the model data.
The paper reports p-values but does not identify a standard-error correction or clustering procedure; no extra cluster variable can be inferred.
No regression weights are reported. Asset weighting is part of construction of selected industry controls (diversification, ownership, R&D), not a fit weight.
Generalized least squares with time-random effects is reported for the frozen baseline; supporting regression estimators, monthly beta fit window, and some variable aggregations remain unspecified.
Preserve the stated sample exclusions, CUSIP duplicate removal, segment-based SIC assignment, top/bottom two firm selection within four-digit SIC, and high-minus-low pool aggregation.

implementation_issues.description: The four supporting regressions’ exact estimators and the monthly beta model’s daily estimation window are not reported; the paper’s equations and labels are preserved without inferring OLS or a beta window.

The paper conflicts on the order of logging and averaging the inflation-adjusted size measure and on beta-volatility aggregation (firm-level standard deviations versus variances of monthly betas). These source alternatives remain unresolved.

The study uses the legacy seasonally adjusted finished-goods PPI series and an historical Compustat/CRSP vintage. Current BLS/Compustat/CRSP data revisions may change the underlying series; no direct replacement is assumed.

review_notes: The 1983–1995 matched-industry baseline fit period is retained. Future earnings/dividend terms extend raw data to 1998, while the five-year EPS-volatility window plus its inner prior-year earnings/price denominator extends backward to 1977.
The source explicitly notes fiscal/calendar year asynchronicity; annual accounting variables are not silently aligned to calendar-year return variation.

design_coverage.reason: Construct the original firm-year universe by CRSP/Compustat matched records from 1983–1995; delete non-10/11 CUSIP suffix duplicates; assign SIC from the sales-largest business segment; exclude financials and utilities; require uninterrupted weekly-return years; then build four-digit high/low and two-digit industry-year pools.
Use dated GVKEY–PERMNO links and dated segment/company identifiers; sampled fields do not establish historical link completeness.
The baseline uses time-random effects; no fixed-effect dummy family is reported. The time-random-effects panel/year grouping and industry-year inputs are part of the model data.
The paper reports p-values but does not identify a standard-error correction or clustering procedure; no extra cluster variable can be inferred.
No regression weights are reported. Asset weighting is part of construction of selected industry controls (diversification, ownership, R&D), not a fit weight.
Generalized least squares with time-random effects is reported for the frozen baseline; supporting regression estimators, monthly beta fit window, and some variable aggregations remain unspecified.
Preserve the stated sample exclusions, CUSIP duplicate removal, segment-based SIC assignment, top/bottom two firm selection within four-digit SIC, and high-minus-low pool aggregation.

implementation_issues.description: The four supporting regressions’ exact estimators and the monthly beta model’s daily estimation window are not reported; the paper’s equations and labels are preserved without inferring OLS or a beta window.

The paper conflicts on the order of logging and averaging the inflation-adjusted size measure and on beta-volatility aggregation (firm-level standard deviations versus variances of monthly betas). These source alternatives remain unresolved.

The study uses the legacy seasonally adjusted finished-goods PPI series and an historical Compustat/CRSP vintage. Current BLS/Compustat/CRSP data revisions may change the underlying series; no direct replacement is assumed.

review_notes: The 1983–1995 matched-industry baseline fit period is retained. Future earnings/dividend terms extend raw data to 1998, while the five-year EPS-volatility window plus its inner prior-year earnings/price denominator extends backward to 1977.
The source explicitly notes fiscal/calendar year asynchronicity; annual accounting variables are not silently aligned to calendar-year return variation.
